title: The First Noel
description: The traditional English carol in the four parts of Bramley and Stainer's Christmas Carols New and Old, for 2 to 4 singers: the first two verses, the angel and the star, each with the Nowell chorus, in a gentle three. The tune climbs a whole octave from its low D in the first line, and every chorus sings its four Nowells before "Born is the King of Israel".

licence.arrangement: the four parts of Christmas Carols New and Old, No. VI (unsigned, so the music editor's: John Stainer, died 1901; public domain): Stainer's tune unchanged in his key and metre, and his chords, with these changes for 2 to 4 beginners: every lower part sings one note a syllable where Stainer moves within one (20 places: the alto's "night" and chorus "ell", the tenor's quavers under "The", "In", "Now-", "did", "their", "they" and the chorus, the bass's under "ell", "fields", "they", "was", "Is-" and the chorus); the alto takes the chord's third where Stainer's alto doubles the tune's root or fifth: C#4 under the tune's A4 on "ell" and "they" (beats 4 and 28, his E4), F#4 under "An-", "cer-", "shep-", "keep-", "cold" and "night" (7, 13, 16, 31, 37, 40, his A4), C#4 under the tune's G4 before each cadence (21, 45, 69, his E4); the alto sings A3 for the opening "The" (his D4); the tenor exchanges where the alto moves (F#3 on "The" and on each "Now-" and "where" over B, A3 under "ell", "the", "they" and "lay", D4 under "herds", "fields" and "was", E4 under "in", B3 on the chorus's first "ell" (Stainer's own note) and D4 on its "Now-" and A3 under "of"); the bass holds A2 under "ell, the" and "they lay" (4 to 7 and 28 to 31) where Stainer leaps to A3 and makes an E minor chord on G, takes D3 under "An-" and "keep-", A3 under "so", and sings the chorus's climb to D4 an octave lower (G2, B2, D3, B2, A2, G2, D3) and D3 under "Is-", so it stays in a beginner bass's range; verse 2 sung to the same parts, a lower part holding its note through the tune's slurs; in verse 2 the lower parts take E minor 7 then A7 on E under "be-" (beats 92 and 93, where verse 1's tune note is harmonised), so the duet has no seventh against the tune; breaths written in for beginners; accepted exceptions: the alto rises A3, D4, F#4 through the D chord into the chorus's second "ell" (52 and 127), a smoother line than Stainer's C#4, which would only move the same leap; the duet and trio keep a bare fourth, D4 over A3, and the D chord without its third where the tune sits on its lowest note, D4 (beats 1, 25, 49, 76, 100 and 124: no beginner alto reaches F#3, and the F# sounds in the tune just before and after); the A chord with an added ninth where the tune's B4 passes to its C#5 within a syllable (6, 30, 81, 105); and a passing C-sharp half-diminished chord on E between D chords in the duet (15, 39, 114)
licence.source: H. R. Bramley and John Stainer, Christmas Carols New and Old, first series (London: Novello, Ewer and Co.; first series published 1867; this copy a later printing of the 1870s, catalogued [187?], the same copy as God Rest Ye), No. VI, "The First Nowell", pp. 12 and 13, in four parts in D, 3/4, the Chorus marked ff, written here in D in 3/4 as printed; verse 1 and the Chorus as printed under the music, and verse 2 as printed below it ("Nowell, &c." sung as the Chorus), fitted to the notes by us ("saw" over D and C#, "the" over C# and B, "be-" over B and C#, "yond" over D and A, "gave" over D and C#, "ued" and "day" over two notes as "night" and "was" are in verse 1); the long s modernised, "lookèd" kept; the last bar shortened by the pickup's beat and the last "el" given a full stop; read from the University of California Libraries copy at archive.org/details/christmascarolsn00staiiala/page/n17 and n18, its index (n51) giving words and air as "Traditional"; the same music checked against the undated later edition (No. 6, p. 12) at archive.org/details/christmascarolsn00bramuoft/page/n13
